headline: Registry publish is NOT blocked by missing work — only by an EXPIRED token. A fresh device code was already captured. npm is blocked by a dead token. Two user commands unblock both.

user_actions.why: Saved token in ~/.config/mcp-publisher/token.json (method=github, scope io.github.theluckystrike/* + io.github.BeLikeNative/*) expired 2026-09-30 04:20 UTC.
user_actions.what_happens: Prints a device code + https://github.com/login/device; open URL in browser, enter code, authorize. (~2 min)

code_captured_this_session.note: Captured 2026-10-07 10:38 local by starting login in background and killing it. Device codes expire in ~15 min — if you miss the window, just rerun the command to get a fresh code.

user_actions.after_login: Run the publish commands below (5 stale manifests).

user_actions.why: ~/.npmrc token is dead: `npm whoami` -> E401. Blocks publishing 54 @theluckystrike/mcp-* packages (54 package.json in servers/; 'mcp-receipts' appears unscoped — verify before publishing).
user_actions.what_happens: Browser opens; log in to npmjs.com; token is written to ~/.npmrc. Verify with `npm whoami` (should print 'theluckystrike').
user_actions.alternative: Create a granular token at https://www.npmjs.com/settings/theluckystrike/tokens/new (type: Granular, permission Read and write on packages under @theluckystrike) and paste into ~/.npmrc as //registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=<TOKEN>

registry: for n in credit-note delivery-schedule packing-list price-tracker-drop-alert-watch time-tracker-timesheet-billable-hours; do echo $n; done
# Registry already has these 5 names at 0.22.4 while local manifests say 0.22.0 — bump local version to 0.22.5 in servers/<name>/server.json first, then:
for n in credit-note delivery-schedule packing-list price-tracker-drop-alert-watch time-tracker-timesheet-billable-hours; do (cd servers/$n && mcp-publisher publish server.json); done
npm: cd servers/<name> && npm publish --access public   # per package, after bumping version

auth.status: EXPIRED (6 days ago) — this is the only registry blocker

non_interactive_auth_options.dns: non-interactive: `mcp-publisher login dns --domain <domain> --private-key <key>` — requires the user to register a domain in the registry UI and hold a DNS private key; long-term automation option
non_interactive_auth_options.http: non-interactive HTTP auth with --domain; same setup burden
